newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria sets up fund to develop southern provinces.
newsitem.headline: Algeria sets up fund to develop southern provinces.

text.p: Algeria's President Liamine Zeroual said on Sunday the government was to set up a special fund to finance development projects in the country's southern areas.
Zeroual said the fund would channel part of Algeria's oil and gas current taxes to spur economic growth in the southern provinces, mainly free of political opposition to the authorities.
Oil and gas, providing more than half of the state budget and more than 90 of the country's exports, come from fields in the country's southern Sahara Desert provinces.
Zeroual, quoted by the official news agency APS, said the fund would start operating in 1998. He made his announcement one month before Algeria is to hold parliamentary elections.
Zeroual's backers, including his close aides and government ministers, are among about 8,000 candidates standing for the 380-seat National Assembly in the June 5 election.

Algeria has been without an elected parliament since 1992 when the country plunged into violence following the cancellation of a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead. About 60,000 people have been killed.
